chapter: Mingus and the call from Hampton
title: Dinner with Mingus, who plays Monk's bass
summary: Mingus ate at Monk's house, examined his German three-quarter bass and played it masterfully, inspiring rather than discouraging him.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: And, some beautiful stories about Mingus; there must be millions of them. I don't want to add another story about Mingus, but I remember we had a great feast that day. And being the big eater that he is, he really put it away. And it just made me feel so great because he was enjoying not just the company but the purpose. We come to have dinner and with the good, you know, friendship. And it was just thing, just like we were friends. And I always...he was warm like that. I was always hearing different stories about Charlie; well, it would give you a little leery feeling. But he was just the opposite, you know that.

And I remember, he said to me after he finished dinner, he said, 'How you doing with the bass?' And I said, 'Oh, just doing fine.' And I was...the blood was just rushing through my body. He said, 'What kind of bass you got?' I said, 'Well, I got a German bass.' He said, 'Oh, good. What size?' I told him, 'Three-quarter.' 'I want to take a look at it.' So I took him back into my room.

He said, 'Why, this is a nice bass. I like this bass.' And he was examining it, looking at it, and as he turned it and looked at it, looked down inside of it, and 'Oh, boy, this is a nice bass. Feels good, really feels good.' And he started to play it. And he played the bass like he made it, as if he made that instrument.
It was like having a master lesson, hm?

The finesse he had! I was standing there with my mouth open. And here I'm, I know I felt like I was a...you know, in my own home town, for what that was worth, fair bass player. But he erased all of that. It was just like, I felt like going back to the trucks.

How could anybody play an instrument like that, I'm thinking. How could I ever get to be like that? If that... how could I get to be... I couldn't make my hands do that, my mind do that. He went clear down that bass, and across it, and every way, and took the bow and...He didn't like the bow, it wasn't a good bow and I knew that. I couldn't play with it anyhow, but he did everything. And I was...
To me, he was the greatest person I've ever seen. It was just like I never imagined anybody could come and master
something like that, something that I've had some experience with, I'd been spending day in, day out, day in, day out, day in. And he'd come and see it for the first time and just, whew...
Yes, but obviously you didn't go back...

No, I didn't. In fact, I was inspired. I didn't want to play like Mingus. I didn't want to be a Mingus. I didn't want to be a Ray Brown. I love these people, like that. But I wanted to be...to express myself like they expressed themselves.
